junction.name: Frederick Douglass Boulevard & West 145 Street, New York City

claims.text: Frederick Douglass Boulevard & West 145 Street had 17 injury crashes in police records since 2021-10-31: 3 pedestrians injured, 7 cyclists injured and 0 people killed.
These counts are Frederick Douglass Boulevard & West 145 Street's own: the city's record places 124 of the 178 records within 100 m at another intersection or street, and they are left out.
At the U.S. DOT's values that harm costs about $1.2 million a year.
No crash pattern here stands out against the city's priority junctions.

The city's Leading Pedestrian Interval signals: passed the causal gate (pedestrian injury crashes changed -17% (95% interval -22% to -11%) at 1,651 sites against sites treated later or the citywide trend, and a placebo date shows nothing).
The city's turn traffic calming: earlier trend (a simple before/after says -26%, but a placebo date before the work shows a drop too, so the decline cannot be credited to the program).
The city's enhanced crossings: not shown (at 96 sites the change in pedestrian injury crashes (-7%, 95% interval -50% to +69%) could be zero).
The city's speed humps: not shown (at 1,008 sites the change in injury crashes (+0%, 95% interval -9% to +9%) could be zero).

Backplates with Retroreflective Borders would avoid about 0.5 crashes a year (CMF 1410, the record FHWA's fact sheet cites; evidence: only if a site check confirms it), worth $175,000 a year; check on site: an entry on yellow or red.

Yellow Change Intervals would avoid about 0.3 crashes a year (CMF 4219, the more conservative of the two middle records of 4; evidence: only if a site check confirms it), worth $91,000 a year; check on site: an entry on yellow or red; the current yellow plus all-red time is below the ITE recommended practice.
The NYC Department of Transportation (NYC DOT) is responsible for Frederick Douglass Boulevard, West 145 Street (not listed in NYSDOT Roadway Inventory, so a city street).
Who can push for it: Council Member, District 9, New York City Council; Manhattan Community Board 10.
A request letter to the NYC Department of Transportation (NYC DOT) is drafted and checked.

draft_request.letter:
To: the NYC Department of Transportation (NYC DOT)
Cc: Council Member, District 9, New York City Council; Manhattan Community Board 10
Subject: Request for safety study at Frederick Douglass Boulevard & West 145 Street

Dear colleagues at NYC DOT,

We are writing to ask that you carry out a safety study at the junction of Frederick Douglass Boulevard & West 145 Street.

The official record for the 5 years from 31 October 2021 shows 29 crashes, including 17 injury crashes. Among those hurt were 3 pedestrians and 7 cyclists. No one was recorded as killed. The record lists this location as a city priority location. Using the U.S. DOT's official values for the cost of crashes (2024 dollars), the harm is valued at $1.2 million per year. No safety work is recorded in this period; the latest recorded safety project was a Leading Pedestrian Interval signal in 2018.

We ask you to consider, on the roads you are responsible for, the following fixes where a site check shows they are suitable:

- reflective backplates on the traffic signals, which is expected to prevent 0.5 injury crashes per year and avoid $175,000 in harm per year. A site check is needed for an entry on yellow or red.

- longer yellow signal times, which is expected to prevent 0.3 injury crashes per year and avoid $91,000 in harm per year. A site check is needed for an entry on yellow or red, and to check whether the current yellow plus all-red time is below the ITE recommended practice.

Please let us know the outcome of the study and what steps will follow.

Yours sincerely,

[Your name]
[Your organisation or address]
